record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: What are the fundamental privacy-accuracy trade-offs for user-level differential privacy in federated learning when users contribute highly unequal amounts of data, and how should user contributions be clipped or bounded adaptively in that setting?

evidence.quote: Hence, similar to recent works on user-level DP in the central model [21], ﬁguring out how to adaptively bound the contributions of users and clip the model parameters remains an interesting research direction [446, 377]. More broadly, unlike record-level DP where fundamental trade-offs between accuracy and privacy are well understood for a variety of canonical learning and estimation tasks, user-level DP is fundamentally less understood ... Thus, more work needs to be done to better understand the fundamental trade-offs in this emerging setting of DP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a population of users $u = 1, \ldots, n$ each hold local datasets $D_u$ of possibly very different sizes $|D_u|$, and a central server iteratively trains a model $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ by aggregating per-user updates $\Delta_u(\theta)$. The training procedure is required to satisfy user-level $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differential privacy, meaning that the distribution over the released model (or sequence of models) is $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-indistinguishable when an arbitrary single user's entire dataset $D_u$ is replaced. A standard mechanism enforces this by clipping each per-user update to have $\ell_2$-norm at most $C$ and adding Gaussian noise calibrated to $C$.

(a) Determine the fundamental information-theoretic trade-offs between accuracy and user-level differential privacy in this setting when the data-per-user distribution $\{|D_u|\}_{u=1}^n$ is highly heterogeneous. Specifically, for canonical learning and estimation tasks (e.g., mean estimation of a bounded random variable, stochastic convex optimization, and empirical risk minimization on Lipschitz losses), characterize tight upper and lower bounds on the achievable excess risk (or estimation error) as a function of $n$, $\varepsilon$, $\delta$, and the empirical distribution of $\{|D_u|\}$.

(b) Design and analyze a procedure that adaptively chooses, for each user $u$ and each round $t$, a clipping bound $C_{u,t}$ (and corresponding model-parameter or update bound) so as to:
  (i) satisfy user-level $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-differential privacy for the entire training procedure, and
  (ii) achieve excess risk matching the lower bounds from (a) up to constants or polylogarithmic factors,
without requiring a priori knowledge of the per-user update-norm distribution or the data-size distribution.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a research direction rather than a single sharp conjecture. While there is substantial recent work proposing adaptive clipping heuristics (e.g., quantile-based adaptive clipping by Andrew et al., ULDP-AVG/SGD for cross-silo user-level DP, and various adaptive-clipping FL schemes from 2023–2025), tight characterizations of the fundamental privacy–accuracy trade-offs for user-level DP under highly unequal user contributions, and provably optimal adaptive clipping schemes matching such bounds, are not established. The broad direction therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Differentially Private Learning with Adaptive Clipping
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes clipping at an online-estimated quantile of the per-user update norm distribution, but does not provide tight trade-off bounds for unequal user data sizes.
status_evidence.claim: Adaptive clipping methods exist as heuristics, but optimality with respect to fundamental user-level DP trade-offs is not established.

status_evidence.title: Uldp-FL: Federated Learning with Across-Silo User-Level Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces user-level weighted clipping to bound user-level sensitivity when users contribute unbounded numbers of records, addressing but not resolving heterogeneous-contribution trade-offs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent algorithms address user-level DP under heterogeneous contributions but the fundamental trade-offs remain incompletely understood.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Personalized Federated Learning with Adaptive Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how clients with small updates are dominated by noise while clients near the clipping threshold dominate aggregation, motivating ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: The accuracy–privacy trade-off under unequal user contributions is an active, unresolved research area.
